document.title: Split stories that share one motive into parts
document.summary: The skill now gives each story its own `part` when one motive ties several stories together, and eight new eval cases check it.
document.why: Agents [split a review into parts less often than they could](source:t1).

sources.label: Claude Code session · Nov 7
sources.gist: Agents split into parts too rarely; why-loop on multi-part PRs.

sources.label: Skill: split stories that share one motive into parts
Eval: add parts cases; accept a page-object part in cigster-99

groups.title: What counts as a story
groups.summary: Step 3 defines a story as work that could have been its own PR, and says a shared motive gives one `why`, not one story. `.agents/skills/comprehende/SKILL.md` is the synced copy of `skills-next/comprehende/SKILL.md`.

attention.note: Step 3 now asks the agent to split a retro or cleanup sweep into one part per fix, which can over-split. Two sentences hold it back: "One cause fixed in several places is one story", and small edits of one kind for one reader stay one story. Without the first, the single-bug `flask-6096-planted` case split into 2 parts in 2 of 2 runs.

notes.body: The done check now asks a one-story review to justify each group.
Failing runs quoted this removed sentence to keep a retro in one part.

fileNotes.skills-next/comprehende/SKILL.md: Rewrites the story sentences in step 3 and the step 4 done check; drops one grouping sentence.

groups.title: Cases with one retro motive
groups.summary: Three PRs where one retro motivates independent fixes; each case expects one part per fix. The old skill kept these in one part in 3 of 10 runs.

fileNotes.eval/cases/comprehende-182/case.json: Expects 3 to 5 parts; keeps the three tooling scripts apart.
fileNotes.eval/cases/comprehende-182/expected.md: Must: Pages wait, `check:changed`, and worktree setup are separate parts.
fileNotes.eval/cases/vitadeck-150/case.json: Expects 4 to 8 parts; keeps stb_ds away from the demo count.
fileNotes.eval/cases/vitadeck-150/expected.md: Must not: one part because one retro motivates it.
fileNotes.eval/cases/cigster-144/case.json: Expects 3 to 6 parts; keeps policy, image CI, and goldens apart.
fileNotes.eval/cases/cigster-144/expected.md: Regenerated goldens trail the golden part, not their own story.

groups.title: Cases that announce their split
groups.summary: Five PRs whose title, body, or issues name two independent changes; each case expects two or three parts. The old skill already passed them, so they guard against a regression.

fileNotes.eval/cases/comprehende-143/case.json: Expects 2 to 3 parts; narrow-screen and font files apart.
fileNotes.eval/cases/comprehende-143/expected.md: The title joins two features with "plus".
fileNotes.eval/cases/comprehende-145/expected.md: Hook installer removal and eval artifact retention are unrelated.
fileNotes.eval/cases/vitadeck-127/case.json: Expects 2 to 3 parts and a ticket source.
fileNotes.eval/cases/vitadeck-127/expected.md: One issue lists two items; the reformat stays out of the emoji part.
fileNotes.eval/cases/vitadeck-81/case.json: Expects 2 to 3 parts; `stb_ds.h` apart from the runtime.
fileNotes.eval/cases/vitadeck-81/expected.md: Two issues, two fixes; the dropped-event log may be a third part.
fileNotes.eval/cases/vitadeck-99/expected.md: Two issues: vendored patch record and emoji upload.

groups.title: cigster-99 accepts a refactor part
groups.summary: `eval/cases/cigster-99/expected.md` now accepts the page objects with the migrated visual specs as their own refactor part, and its Must not keeps only the `dependsOn` rule.

attention.note: The skill says a story holds its foundation, and the living-room spec imports `HostPage`, `TvPage`, `RemotePage`, and `PlayerPage`. The case now accepts those page objects in a separate refactor part, because they also carry the visual-spec migration and could have been their own PR first. `case.json` is unchanged, so no expect enforces either grouping.

groups.title: Frozen PR and issue sources
groups.summary: `pnpm eval:add` wrote these JSON captures of each PR, its comments, and linked issues. Skip them: the eval reads them as the sources the skill would fetch.

commits.subject: Skill: split stories that share one motive into parts
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A retro or sweep gives one why, not one story. One cause fixed in several places stays one story. A one-story review says why each group could not have been its own PR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
